authority: 2026-09-10 owner asked why there is a row limit, whether all data is written to Excel, and explicitly requested continuing the next API efficiency work.
objective: Separate lightweight model connection from detailed acquisition and make production force requests retrieve only requested members under caller admission budgets; document the actual external snapshot and worksheet data paths.
bounded_units: A1: trace capture, transport, offline memory and explicit worksheet writes
A2: production per-object force acquisition with preflight and incremental caller row budgets
A3: versioned model-overview contract and worker using existing inspection/lease/journal owners
A4: lightweight Excel connection and explicit detailed-context handoff, with retained legacy routes
A5: focused and installed read-only evidence, documentation and one hosted delivery cycle

acceptance_rows.outcome: Explain that 100000 rows is the current capture/import admission envelope, not an Excel worksheet limit. Full snapshots remain external; import writes references and the explicit review command writes all rows for one selected member, without paging.

The production worker uses exact requested-object force calls, never the All-group route. Minimum required rows are checked before result reads, the caller row budget is enforced during capture, and failure publishes no partial accepted snapshot.

Retained group/bulk capture and snapshot profiles keep their schemas and default limits. The 100000-row/1000-member/encoded-byte admission envelope is not silently increased. One provider object call is explicitly not a hard memory bound.

A separate overview contract binds source, request, counts, available analysis/design state and external evidence. It performs no GetAllPoints/GetAllFrames, per-frame getter loop, table-data or force read and accepts native units as metadata without setting them.

The normal Excel Connect action uses overview; detailed context is an explicit action. Existing direct context APIs remain available with their original semantics. Workbook ownership, cancellation/quiescence, package identity and stale-source checks remain effective.

Focused tests prove selected-only force scope, incremental budgets/no partial acceptance, overview identity/counts/provenance and legacy compatibility. Installed read-only overview measures exact source preservation, calls and elapsed time; a qualified fixture proves scoped forces and an owned Excel workbook proves connection/sheet behavior.

All intended source/test/documentation/evidence writes freeze before routine verification. Required hosted checks and exact candidate integrity pass; no source-model mutation, analysis/design rerun, production add-in installation or release occurs.

non_goals: Unlimited or paged multi-snapshot storage, increasing qualified capacity, or adding worksheet/viewer paging
Changing production engineering admission, user-model result selections/units, source files or analysis/design state
Lifecycle mutation service, production installation or package release
Deleting or updating other worktrees or unrelated user edits
likely_pitfalls: Describing post-call limits as vendor allocation bounds
Disguising an overview as accepted full geometry or beam design input
Losing exact request/source/workbook binding during the overview-to-details handoff
Equating request cancellation with stopped ETABS
Claiming all rows are in worksheets, or claiming existing selected-member review is paged
Inferring live qualification from a build or static method signature

verification.installed: Read-only current-model overview and retained qualified fixture acquisition; isolated owned Excel workbook loaded from a candidate package without changing installed add-ins. Record source equality, no unrequested force calls, cleanup, worksheet counts and exact artifacts.
verification.performance: Per-operation development timings and call counts only; PF9 final certification remains deferred.
verification.fixture_setup: Use a separate copy of the retained analyzed WP11 fixture. Restore its recorded kN-m-C API units and three static output selections only in that owned test instance; do not save or rerun analysis. Record setup calls, source-file equality and owned-instance exit. Production readers and the large user model remain getter-only.
verification.excel_setup: Load the signed development XLL into a new owned Excel instance. Temporarily suppress only the exact installed StructAutomate startup entry, retain its preimage, and restore it in finally. No installed binary or candidate startup registration is written.
